# Design Document Layer System

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/document-layer-apply-undo)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

Create a document-editing system that stores properties for multiple layers.

In this design application, every visual layer is referenced by a unique integer `id`. A layer contains string properties represented by key-value pairs, for example a color, shape, or size. A layer comes into existence automatically when the first property is assigned to its `id`. The document must also be able to undo the latest property assignment.

Implement the `Document` class:

- `Document()` creates a document with no layers initially.
- `void apply(int id, String propertyName, String value)` assigns `value` to `propertyName` on the layer identified by `id`. If that layer has not been seen before, create it implicitly. When the property is already present, replace its existing value.
- `List<String> getLayer(int id)` produces the layer's current properties as strings in the form `"<key>=<value>"`, ordered by key in ascending alphabetical order. For a missing layer or a layer without properties, return an **empty** list.
- `void undo()` cancels the latest `apply` operation. If that operation replaced an existing value, restore the earlier value; if it introduced the property, delete the property instead.

## Constraints

- $$1 \le id \le 10^5$$
- `propertyName` and `value` are non-empty strings.
- `undo()` is invoked only when there is at least one operation available to reverse.
- Every `apply` operation changes exactly one property on exactly one layer.

## Example

> **Input:**
> ["Document", "apply", "getLayer", "apply", "getLayer", "apply", "getLayer", "undo", "getLayer", "undo", "getLayer", "undo", "getLayer"]
> [[], [1, "color", "green"], [1], [2, "shape", "triangle"], [2], [1, "color", "blue"], [1], [], [1], [], [2], [], [1]]
>
> **Output:**
> [null, null, ["color=green"], null, ["shape=triangle"], null, ["color=blue"], null, ["color=green"], null, [], null, []]
>
> **Explanation:**
> - `Document doc = new Document();` // Starts with an empty document.
> - `doc.apply(1, "color", "green");` // Adds the value "green" for "color" on layer 1.
> - `doc.getLayer(1);` // Produces ["color=green"] because layer 1 has that one property.
> - `doc.apply(2, "shape", "triangle");` // Adds "triangle" as layer 2's "shape" value.
> - `doc.getLayer(2);` // Produces ["shape=triangle"] because layer 2 has one property.
> - `doc.apply(1, "color", "blue");` // Changes layer 1's color from "green" to "blue".
> - `doc.getLayer(1);` // Produces ["color=blue"] after the replacement.
> - `doc.undo();` // Reverses the preceding apply, bringing layer 1's color back to "green".
> - `doc.getLayer(1);` // Produces ["color=green"].
> - `doc.undo();` // Reverses the operation that added layer 2's shape, so that property is deleted.
> - `doc.getLayer(2);` // Produces [] because layer 2 no longer has properties.
> - `doc.undo();` // Reverses the first color assignment on layer 1, removing that property.
> - `doc.getLayer(1);` // Produces [] because layer 1 has no remaining properties.
